name: Wan Jie
current_role: Chairman, Artron Art Group (雅昌文化集团), Shenzhen
profile: Beijing-born (1962) founder-chairman of Artron, set up in Shenzhen in 1993 as a high-end art printer. He expanded it into China's largest art-data and online art portal (artron.net) with bases in Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen. A long-time CPPCC National Committee member, he also served as a vice-president of the Palace Museum Academy.
interesting_fact: Artron grew from fine-art book printing into a digital art database business; in 2022 Wan used his CPPCC proposals to push metaverse and digital-culture infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2014 'Two Sessions' he proposed a national copyright-registration system for Chinese calligraphy and paintings to clean up forgery in the art market.

public_contacts.value: help@artron.net (general Artron portal helpdesk, not personal)

notes: Best route is via Artron Group corporate channels; little English-language coverage. Industry listed as Print but now primarily art data/culture.

name: Wang Jinglian
profile: Listed on the 2008 Hurun China Rich List with Jinsheng Group (copper). No reliable online source found linking the name 王景连 to a specific Jinsheng group or role, so identity could not be confirmed.
notes: Could not verify. A copper business called Shandong Jinsheng Nonferrous Group (Linyi) went through a court-supervised restructuring/settlement in 2022-23 (https://www.zhonglun.com/news/trade/15361.html), but no source names Wang Jinglian in connection with it. Treat as unverified; low priority.

name: Maroš Grund
current_role: Senior Research Fellow and Member of the Board, ESET (Bratislava)
profile: Slovak software engineer and co-owner of cybersecurity firm ESET, maker of NOD32 antivirus. He became a co-owner in 2005 alongside Richard Marko and co-authored ESET's new-generation detection engine; he stepped back from day-to-day management in 2011 but remains on the board as Senior Research Fellow.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he and fellow ESET shareholder Peter Kusý bought Bratislava's landmark Carlton Hotel building in a joint venture with developer Erik Mikurčík.
deep_cut_fact: ESET's own 30th-anniversary history credits him (with Richard Marko) as co-author of the new generation of ESET's detection engine, the core of its products.
notes: Low public profile; engineer rather than spokesperson. Best route is via ESET's newsroom/press team. Owners stepping back from daily management in 2011: https://www.virusbulletin.com/blog/2011/01/all-change-top-eset/

name: Wang Yanzhi
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Gaea Mobile / 盖娅互娱 (Beijing/Shenzhen game publisher); latest-role sources are older
profile: Chinese mobile-game publisher. After stints at Kunlun and other game firms he founded Lemeng Interactive in 2012, sold it to Zhongqing Longtu (Locojoy) in 2013 and built its publishing arm as COO. He then founded Gaea, a game publisher focused on overseas markets, in which he controls about 77%.
interesting_fact: As Longtu's COO he signed the hit mobile game 'Dota Legends' (刀塔传奇), which pushed Longtu into China's top-10 game publishers.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Lemeng Interactive (乐檬互动, founded 2012), was fully acquired by Zhongqing Longtu within about a year (May 2013), and its team became the core of Longtu's mobile publishing division.
notes: Gaea Mobile (盖娅互娱) is listed on China's NEEQ/BSE as 430181; company filings are the best source for an official contact. No personal social accounts found. Current status (2024+) not verified.

name: Guan Yanbin
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Kuihua (Sunflower) Pharmaceutical; no executive role since 2019
profile: Heilongjiang entrepreneur who turned a failing county brick/plastics factory into a business, then in 1998 led 46 shareholders in buying the insolvent state-owned Wuchang Pharmaceutical, which became Kuihua (Sunflower) Pharmaceutical, a major OTC and children's medicine maker. He resigned as chairman in 2019; reports say he remains the controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: In April 1998 he and 45 other individuals paid about RMB14.9m for Wuchang Pharmaceutical, which had been shut for nine months and was insolvent, and built it into a listed national brand.
deep_cut_fact: Early in China's reform era he voluntarily left a government office job to run a near-bankrupt small brick factory, switched it to plastic products, and in 1985 borrowed money to import equipment from Italy.
notes: IMPORTANT: In July 2020 a Daqing court convicted him of intentional homicide (case involving his ex-wife) and sentenced him to 11 years (https://finance.sina.cn/2020-07-17/detail-iivhvpwx5932813.d.html). He is likely in prison; not a suitable podcast guest. Kuihua is now run by other executives.

name: Graham Tuckwell
current_role: Founder and Chairman, ETFS Capital (UK); Chairman, ETF Shares
profile: Canberra-born ANU economics/law graduate who worked in mining finance (Salomon Brothers, Normandy Mining) before launching Gold Bullion Securities in 2003, one of the first physically backed gold exchange-traded products. He built ETF Securities into a ~US$30bn issuer, sold most of it to WisdomTree and others, and now backs fintech/crypto via ETFS Capital (21Shares, etf.com).
interesting_fact: He and wife Louise gave A$50m to ANU in 2013, later raised to A$100m, to fund the Tuckwell Scholarship; he was made an Officer of the Order of Australia (AO) in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an adviser to economist Vince FitzGerald in the Department of the Prime Minister, and as an ANU student lived at Bruce Hall.

public_contacts.value: Previous guest on Equity Mates podcast ('a pioneer of the ETF revolution')

notes: Good podcast candidate: has done long-form podcast interviews before. Australian, Melbourne/London based. Has mining-finance background relevant to energy/commodities angle.

name: Albert Erani
current_role: Major shareholder (10%+ owner), Organogenesis Holdings (NASDAQ: ORGO); co-founder and VP/Secretary, A & E Stores, Inc.; principal, Rugby Realty Co.
profile: New Jersey-based retail and real-estate businessman who co-founded A & E Stores with his cousin Alan Ades in the early 1970s. The Ades-Erani group took regenerative-medicine firm Organogenesis private when it emerged from bankruptcy in 2002-03 and rebuilt it into a listed wound-care company; he is a former Organogenesis director and his son David now sits on the board.
interesting_fact: After Organogenesis' 2002 Chapter 11, its staff fell from about 125 to roughly 15; the investor group led by Alan Ades (which included the Erani family) revived it into a Nasdaq-listed company.
notes: Very private; no interviews or personal online presence found. Age not public but active in business since 1971, so likely elderly; alive status unconfirmed. Best route is via Organogenesis IR. Bio details from https://www.insidertrades.com/organogenesis-holdings-inc-stock/albert-erani

name: Dai Kebin
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Tongdao Liepin Group (HKEX: 6100)
profile: Born in the 1980s, he studied finance at Sun Yat-sen University (2003) and spent five years at P&G before founding a headhunting site that became Liepin, China's leading mid-to-senior talent recruitment platform. He took it public in Hong Kong in 2018, renamed it Tongdao Liepin in 2022, launched overseas brand Leapin from Hong Kong in 2023 and is pushing AI interview products.
interesting_fact: Liepin's 'BHC' model connects Businesses, Headhunters and Candidates; its 2018 IPO was billed as Hong Kong's first technology HR stock. Fortune China has named him to its 40 Under 40 list three times.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he scrapped Liepin's original offline headhunting model and went fully online, despite a painful revenue dip. He told 36Kr: 'Entrepreneurs cannot blame their failures on the winter' (创业者不能把做得不成功的原因归结于寒冬).
notes: A visible speaker (e.g. HK Global Talent Summit), so a podcast request is plausible. AI-in-hiring angle fits the data-center theme. The 2011 pivot is described at https://www.huxiu.com/article/18361.html

name: Zhang Banghui
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and Chairman, Tianbang Food (天邦食品, SZ: 002124); president role reportedly ended April 2026
profile: Born 1963, a former fisheries research assistant who became deputy GM at a Wuxi animal-nutrition company and then general manager of Yuyao Tianbang. He built Tianbang (Tech-Bank) from aquafeed into one of China's larger hog producers and pork processors. After heavy debt in the pork-cycle downturn, the company went through a court-led debt restructuring in 2024.
interesting_fact: In a 2024 interview he predicted the end of China's famous 'pig cycle' as small farmers exit: 'From now on there will be no pig cycle; whoever is cost-competitive will survive.'
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he was a research assistant at the Freshwater Fisheries Research Center of the Chinese Academy of Fishery Sciences in Wuxi; Tianbang's roots are in aquaculture feed.
notes: Hurun 'Tech-bank' = Tianbang (天邦). Company had debt restructuring in 2024 (ST status), so wealth likely much reduced; approach sensitively. Contact via company IR/board secretary listed in SZSE filings.

name: Wu Yibing
profile: Harvard biochemistry PhD who became a McKinsey senior partner and head of its Beijing office, then led Lenovo's acquisition and integration of IBM's PC business as chief strategy officer. He ran CITIC Private Equity from 2009 and joined Temasek in 2013, where he leads its China investment teams.
interesting_fact: At Lenovo he led the acquisition and integration of IBM's PC business, one of the landmark Chinese cross-border tech deals.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a scientist: a BSc in molecular biology from the University of Science and Technology of China and a PhD in biochemistry from Harvard. He also sits on the board of the China Social Entrepreneur Foundation and has served on the Gavi vaccine alliance board.
notes: A professional investor, not a founder; his Hurun listing likely reflects CITIC PE/Goldstone-era wealth. Frequent conference speaker (Milken, Boao), so outreach via Temasek media relations is feasible.

name: MAM Ramaswamy
profile: Died 2 December 2015 in Chennai, aged 84. Former Chairman of the Chettinad Group (Chettinad Cement), Raja of Chettinad and Rajya Sabha member for Karnataka (2004-2010).
notes: Deceased; source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._A._M._Ramaswamy (citing Sathiyam News obituary https://web.archive.org/web/20151208104035/http://sathiyamnews.com/districts/chennai/industrialist-m-m-ramaswamy-passes-away-84). Chettinad Cement is now run by other family members; skip.

name: Li Mingyan
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Shouxiangu Pharmaceutical (寿仙谷, SH: 603896)
profile: Correct characters are 李明焱 (list shows 李明炎). From a family of traditional medicine practitioners in Wuyi, Zhejiang, he built Shouxiangu, a 'China Time-honored Brand', into a listed maker of reishi (lingzhi) mushroom and broken-wall spore powder products. His two sons now serve as vice chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: He helped drive international standards for traditional Chinese medicine on lingzhi (2018) and on broken-wall Ganoderma spore powder (ISO, 2025).
deep_cut_fact: From 1993 he combed the mountains of Zhejiang, Fujian and Jiangxi, collecting 50+ wild reishi strains. He bred 'Xianzhi No.1' around 2001, then sent seeds aboard China's first crewed spacecraft Shenzhou-5 to breed the improved 'Xianzhi No.2' (2006).
notes: Scientist-entrepreneur profile; open to media about TCM standardisation. Contact via the company's SSE-listed IR/board secretary. Not an energy/data-center fit.

name: Alex Saab
current_role: In US federal custody; pleaded guilty to money laundering in Miami (Sept 2026)
profile: Colombian-born businessman who became a key financier and later minister for Venezuela's Maduro government, accused by US prosecutors of laundering proceeds of the CLAP food programme and oil deals. Released in a 2023 prisoner swap, he was detained again in Venezuela in 2026, deported to the US in May 2026 and pleaded guilty on 15 Sept 2026.
notes: NOT a suitable outreach target: currently in US custody after a guilty plea (https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/maduro-ally-alex-saab-pleads-guilty-federal-money-136465836). Wealth figure is from Wikidata and unverified. Recommend skipping.

name: Shu Longsheng
current_role: Vice Chairman (since 2019) and major shareholder, Anhui Xinlong Electrical, now CEC Xingfa/中电鑫龙 (SZ: 002298), Wuhu
profile: Born 1963, a senior engineer who was chairman of Wuhu-based Xinlong Electrical, a maker of switchgear and power-distribution equipment, from 1998 to end-2018 and took it public in Shenzhen. He became vice chairman in 2019 as the company expanded into smart-city and information businesses; he has gradually reduced his stake (about 8% in 2020).
interesting_fact: Before Xinlong he ran the Wuhu Electrical Equipment Factory (芜湖市电器设备厂) as factory director, the base of what became the listed power-equipment group.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a technician at the Tongling phosphate-ammonium fertilizer plant (铜陵市磷铵厂) before moving into electrical equipment.
notes: Power-distribution equipment angle fits an energy/grid podcast. Little media profile; contact via the listed company's board secretary (SZSE filings). Stake reduction: https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-05-22/5f8c64b4-1256-4741-a917-5bfe91ea8c1d.PDF
